text: Type hints tell you and your tools exactly what a function expects.
Name is a string, times is an integer defaulting to one, and it returns a string.
Python doesn't enforce any of this at runtime — it's documentation your editor can check.
They cost you nothing at runtime and save you real time when the code grows.
The body repeats the greeting and strips the trailing space.
Variables take annotations too. Scores is a dict mapping string to int.
Top is a list of strings, built by a comprehension over the items.
Anyone reading line five now knows what's inside without running a thing.
Calling greet with just a name uses the default and greets once.
Pass three and you get it three times, and top gives us the high scorers.
Run mypy over this file and it checks every one of those promises for you.
